newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ headline inflation up 2.4 pct in Sept year.
newsitem.headline: NZ headline inflation up 2.4 pct in Sept year.

text.p: New Zealand's Consumer Price Index rose by 0.6 percent in the September quarter and 2.4 percent in the year to September, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.
Fourteen economists polled by Reuters had expected on average a 0.86 percent quarterly rise for a 2.6 percent annual rise.
Credit services made the largest contribution to the CPI's quarterly increase, recording a rise of 3.6 percent. SNZ said this was mostly due to mortgage interest rates rising 4.0 percent.
It was the second consecutive increase in the Mortgage Interest Index.

The All Groups excluding Credit Services Index rose by 0.4 percent in the quarter, and since the year-ago quarter has risen 2.3 percent. This is the index from which the Reserve Bank's Policy Targets Agreement is derived.
The Superannuitants Price Index for all households rose 0.5 percent in the quarter, and by 2.3 percent over the year.
SNZ said price rises in tobacco and alcohol also contributed to the CPI's rise.
Food prices rose 0.8 percent in the quarter, with grocery foods leading the rise. Meat prices rose for the first time this year.
Housing costs were up 0.6 percent in the quarter, which SNZ said was driven mostly by an increase in rentals of houses and flats, and local authority rates.
Domestic and international airfares fell along with the price of used and new cars, while the cost of vehicle insurance rose. -- Wellington newsroom (64 4) 473 4746
